name: Jaxon Flowers
strengths: Flowers is still the dual-threat QB on the 2025 Bolles reel (#7, shotgun) — he takes the shot: deep sideline ball, receiver in stride, gone.
Flowers keeps it and runs away from the secondary. Designed keep / draw: cut inside, long stride, DBs never close. The close speed is the safety trait.
Flowers will throw it on the run. Flush left, ball over the top across his body. Raw arm, off-platform, still gets there.
Flowers’ own sophomore title card stamps 31 TDs (14 pass / 17 rush). Production matches a run-first dual-threat reel, not a pocket passer.
weaknesses: Flowers’ Hudl is sophomore QB tape only — no safety snaps, so backpedal, hip flip, coverage, and tackle technique cannot be claimed from this cut.
Flowers’ pass reps lean deep go/post vs beaten coverage and off-platform throws. Tight-window intermediate anticipation is thin on the reel.
comparison: Flowers comps to a lighter Grant Delpit mold — listed 6-3 / 185 vs Delpit’s ~6-3 / 208 (same height, leaner frame still filling). Then matching long-stride close speed and open-field vision from the QB reel. Not the finished LSU coverage product, and this tape has no DB snaps.
projection: Flowers projects to develop at safety after the QB-to-DB move: Year 1 learn the back end, Year 2 compete for FS / nickel packages, Year 3+ starter-upside range safety if coverage and tackle catch the 6-3 play speed.
schemeFit: Flowers fits a range free safety who can close from the hash. Conversion athlete first. Do not sell him as a finished cover safety off this reel.

angle: Lead with Florida at No. 1 plus the QB reel close speed that explains the safety chase. Honest: no DB snaps on the Hudl.
